components.css: .ds-tabbar{position:relative;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(5,1fr);max-width:440px;padding:5px;border-radius:999px;background:rgba(250,250,252,.72);-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(24px) saturate(190%);backdrop-filter:blur(24px) saturate(190%);box-shadow:0 12px 36px rgba(0,0,0,.12),0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.06),inset 0 0 0 .5px rgba(255,255,255,.7);isolation:isolate;font-family:-apple-system,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-ind{position:absolute;z-index:0;top:5px;bottom:5px;left:5px;width:calc((100% - 10px)/5);border-radius:999px;background:rgba(118,118,128,.12);transition:transform .5s cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)}.ds-tabbar button{position:relative;z-index:1;height:54px;border:0;background:none;border-radius:999px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:1px;font-size:10px;font-weight:500;color:#666670;cursor:pointer;transition:transform .12s}.ds-tabbar button:active{transform:scale(.9)}.ds-tabbar button[aria-current]{color:#1D7333;font-weight:600}.ds-tabbar svg{width:26px;height:26px;fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.7;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round}.ds-disc{width:50px;height:50px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;background:conic-gradient(#1D7333 40%,color-mix(in srgb,#1D7333 22%,transparent) 0)}.ds-disc>span{width:42px;height:42px;border-radius:50%;background:#1D7333;color:#fff;display:grid;place-items:center;box-shadow:0 4px 12px color-mix(in srgb,#1D7333 45%,transparent)}.ds-disc svg.fill{width:20px;height:20px;fill:currentColor;stroke:none;margin-left:1px}.ds-tabbar button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #1D7333;outline-offset:2px}

narrative.overview:
The Cut should be indistinguishable from something Apple shipped next to Fitness and Reminders. It borrows iOS 26 wholesale rather than interpreting it: system SF faces, the grouped-list surface model (grey ground, white rounded cards, hairline separators), Reminders round ticks, Activity-style rings, a floating glass tab bar, bottom sheets with a grabber, spring motion and haptics. One green accent carries every interactive and "done" state; everything else is system grey.

Density is phone-native: 16px page margins, 44pt targets, one column capped at 560px. At 900px and up (MacBook Air) the same content gets a 220px sidebar in place of the tab bar, a 680px column and centred sheets. All CSS lives in the single <style> in index.html, appended in layers; later blocks override earlier ones, so read the whole cascade before changing a selector.
keyCharacteristics: System fonts only; numerals in SF Rounded with tabular figures.
Grouped lists: bg ground, card surfaces at 22px, 0.5px line separators.
One accent (green); Apple system hues used as fills and status, never as small text.
Glass (blur + saturate) only on floating chrome: tab bar, coach pill, compact nav bar, toast.
Spring easing, press-scale feedback, haptic on completion; all of it off under reduced motion.
Every size in rem (1rem = 17px) so the app follows iOS Text Size.

rules.name: The Fill-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: Apple system hues (orange, red, ring*) are fills. Any text or icon glyph in that hue uses orange-text, red-text, accent or mute, which hold 4.5:1 in light mode. Outlines that carry meaning use tick (3:1).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Green is the only interactive colour. Status uses orange and red; nothing else gets a hue.

rules.name: The Token-Both-Modes Rule
rules.body: A new colour is a new custom property in :root and in the dark override block, never a literal in a component.

rules.name: The Follow-Text-Size Rule
rules.body: All type is rem. html is 17px; on iOS it is font: -apple-system-body, so the whole app tracks Settings > Text Size. Never set a px font size outside SVG.

rules.name: The Capped-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Fixed chrome caps its growth with min(rem, px): tab bar labels, week pills, nav bar, heatmap months.

rules.name: The Rounded-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Figures that are data use --rounded, weight 600-700, tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Glass-Is-Chrome Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter (blur 20-24px, saturate 180-190%) belongs only to floating chrome: tab bar, coach pill, compact nav bar, toast. Content surfaces are opaque.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: Sheets dim the page with rgba(0,0,0,.4 * --dim); dragging the sheet lowers --dim in step.

dos: Do put new colours in :root and the dark block, and use orange-text/red-text/mute/accent for any coloured text.
Do size type in rem against the 17px root, and cap fixed chrome with min(rem, px).
Do give every control a 44pt hit area; extend with a transparent pseudo-element rather than enlarging the drawn shape.
Do use fill for neutral control backgrounds and soft for positive tints.
Do use --spring for anything that moves in space, and gate every animation behind prefers-reduced-motion in CSS and calm() in JS.
Do open new sheets through showSheet() and close through fadeOut() so focus, inert and drag reset stay correct.
Do draw icons as inline line SVGs (24 viewBox, round caps, currentColor).
Do bump VERSION in sw.js whenever index.html changes.
donts: Don't set text in orange, red or ring*; they fail contrast in light mode.
Don't add shadows to cards or rows; elevation is for floating chrome only.
Don't add another backdrop-filter surface on phone; four (tab bar, coach pill, nav bar, toast) is already the budget.
Don't introduce a font beyond the three system stacks or a second accent hue.
Don't use emoji as icons in new UI.
